references.text: The preceding context describing the command to wash hands and feet at the bronze basin, of which verse 21 is a continuation.
The warning that Aaron and his sons must wear the proper garments when entering the tent of meeting so they do not incur guilt and die—the same serious consequence as failing to wash.
The fulfillment of the command where Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet at the bronze basin.
The expression 'a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations' (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם) is used in a similar way.
A perpetual statute through the generations concerning the service of the Levites.
In the New Testament, the image of being washed with clean water is used as a symbol of spiritual cleansing, pointing back to the Levitical purification rituals.
Jesus washes his disciples' feet and explains the necessity of being washed to have a share with him—an echo of the priests' necessary purification.
Both establish a perpetual statute regarding ritual washing to avoid death or impurity in connection with holy service.
Both verses state the same theological principle: priests must keep God's commands to avoid incurring sin and death.
Both establish a perpetual statute concerning washing to deal with ritual impurity in connection with sacred rituals.
